text: What is GSE309890 about, and what files can I actually download?

Abstract
GEO Series GSE309890 examines how the antidepressant sertraline influences the emergence of antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655. The study profiled gene-expression changes by high-throughput RNA-seq in six samples (three sertraline-adapted populations after 40 days evolution and three untreated controls) on platform GPL24659. GEO metadata (UID 200309890) indicate a focus on metabolic rewiring toward the pentose-phosphate pathway (PPP) and a redox-linked mechanism underlying biased resistance to rifampicin and ciprofloxacin. No PubMed article is yet linked. Downloadable content is limited to one compressed CSV matrix (FPKM values for all samples) hosted in the GEO FTP “suppl” directory (510 KB). This file contains the processed expression values required for downstream analysis; raw sequencing data reside in SRA under BioProject PRJNA1363958 (not included here). The present report documents the record’s scope, sample composition, and the exact file location for data acquisition.

I. Introduction
Background. Sertraline, a widely used selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), has been implicated in promoting bacterial antibiotic resistance. Understanding the transcriptional changes underlying this phenomenon is crucial for developing counter-measures such as metabolic adjuvants.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. Prior to consulting GEO, the availability and nature of transcriptomic data for sertraline-induced resistance in E. coli were unclear.
Objective & Hypothesis. Retrieve and summarise the GSE309890 record to identify its experimental design and enumerate downloadable data files, hypothesising that GEO supplies processed expression matrices suitable for re-analysis.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We queried GEO via the geo_series tool to obtain curated metadata and file listings for accession GSE309890, requesting supplementary file details.
Materials. Database: NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), accessed through the MCP geo_series wrapper.
Procedures.
• Tool call: geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=TRUE)  
  – Returns series metadata, FTP directory, and supplementary_file list.
Statistical Analysis. Descriptive only: counts of samples and files were read directly from fields “sample_count” and “supplementary_files”.

III. Results
Data Presentation.
Table 1 – Key attributes of GEO Series GSE309890  
| Attribute | Value |  
|-----------|-------|  
| UID | 200309890 |  
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |  
| Organism | Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 |  
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |  
| Platform | GPL24659 |  
| Samples (total) | 6 (3 control, 3 sertraline-adapted) |  
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |  
| Linked PubMed IDs | none |  
| Supplementary file count | 1 |  

Table 2 – Supplementary files available  
| File name | Size | URL (FTP/HTTPS) | Note |  
|-----------|------|-----------------|-------|  
| GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | 510 KB | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz | Processed expression (FPKM) matrix |

Findings.
1. GSE309890 comprises six RNA-seq samples contrasting sertraline-evolved and control E. coli populations.  
2. GEO provides one downloadable processed file (FPKM counts) of 510 KB.  
3. No raw sequencing files are present in the GEO “suppl” directory; raw reads are presumably in SRA under PRJNA1363958.  
4. No PubMed article is currently linked to the study.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The study supplies a compact processed expression matrix that enables immediate differential-expression or pathway analyses of the sertraline-induced metabolic shift without requiring raw FASTQ processing. The absence of a linked publication suggests data precede formal journal reporting.
Context. The metadata highlight PPP activation and redox modulation as putative drivers of antibiotic resistance, aligning with broader interest in metabolism-based adjuvant strategies.
Limitations. GEO metadata do not include raw read links; additional SRA queries are needed for raw data. Absence of PubMed linkage limits validation of study conclusions.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 offers accessible processed RNA-seq data for investigating sertraline’s impact on E. coli metabolism and resistance. Future work should retrieve the corresponding SRA runs (via PRJNA1363958) to allow re-alignment, and monitor PubMed for forthcoming peer-reviewed publication.

References
[1] NCBI GEO. GSE309890 record summary. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] GEO FTP supplementary file listing. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz  

Acknowledgments
We acknowledge the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus for providing the dataset and file hosting infrastructure.
